sweep_j_strip_phase.evidence: SWEEP-J per ADR-0064 follow-on to SWEEP-I. Three slices investigated; one applied content-stripping (J-2 Helm), two surfaced honest no-op findings (J-1 Cedar, J-3 Kustomize). Slice J-1 (Cedar): zero non-commented entity/action declarations exist across 150 per-µservice .cedar files — Sweep-I already prevented duplicates by keeping all canonical entity/action declarations as documentation comments in cedar-canonical-imports.cedar. Nothing structural to strip; per-µservice files already contain ONLY µservice-specific permit/forbid rules. Slice J-2 (Helm): extended _helpers.tpl with seven new drop-in helpers (securityContext.restrictedContainer, securityContext.restrictedContainerInline, securityContext.podStandard65534, securityContext.podStandard65532, probes.httpHealthLiveness8080, probes.httpHealthReadiness8080, probes.healthzLiveness, probes.healthzReadiness) that exactly match the inline blocks used across two template patterns (Pattern A: single-deployment templates with named-port probes + container-level UID/group; Pattern B: range-tuple multi-deployment templates with pod-level UID 65534 + container-level inline-collection capabilities). 24 deployment.yaml files refactored to call `{{ include "oya.X" $ }}` for these blocks: workflow-studio/visual-canvas-rest, sheets/visual-grid-rest (Pattern A); meet, tasks, notes, translate, social, shorts, network, community, messenger (Pattern B); cell/scheduler, foundry/runtime, application/shell-app, audit-chain/audit-storage, cloud-iac/helm-controller, cloud-k8s/istio-base, cloud-secrets/openbao, forms/response-search-meilisearch, governance/lane-runner-pool, observability/alloy, ontology/cedar-policy-engine, tenancy/citus, workflow-engine/clickhouse (substrate /healthz+/livez probes). Slice J-3 (Kustomize): canonical namespace-restricted-profile component bundled placeholder namespace.yaml/serviceaccount.yaml that would conflict with per-µservice namespace.yaml resources (which carry µservice-specific labels like oyatie.dev/microservice, oyatie.dev/invariants, oyatie/owning-axis the canonical cannot enumerate). Migrated component from "bundle resources" to "commonLabels overlay only" pattern; deleted placeholder namespace.yaml + serviceaccount.yaml from canonical. Per-µservice overlays surveyed: zero overlay has duplicate commonAnnotations matching pack-overlay-canonical/<pack> — overlays use configMapGenerator with per-µservice literal keys plus µservice-specific patches; canonical's commonAnnotations would be ADDITIVE (new metadata), not duplicate-stripping. Per-µservice base/kustomization.yaml files surveyed: zero base has duplicate istio-injection or pod-security-restricted labels in commonLabels — those labels live in per-µservice namespace.yaml; composing the canonical component would ADD them to every resource (also additive, not strip). Honest conclusion: Sweep-I's J-3 canonical components are additive, not deduplicative, against the current per-µservice file shapes. Adopting them is a separate "harmonize-pack-annotations" task, not a stripping task. Helm template line delta: -162 lines across 24 deployment.yaml files (296 deletions vs 186 insertions including canonical helper expansion). Canonical namespace-restricted-profile component lines: -20 (deleted placeholder namespace.yaml + serviceaccount.yaml; simplified kustomization.yaml header). Net Sweep-J line delta: -182 lines across 27 files.

slice_j2_helm.honest_finding: Refactored helpers are TRUE drop-in replacements: byte-equivalent rendered YAML output. Skipped service.yaml/pdb.yaml/servicemonitor.yaml refactor because oya.selectorLabels emits `app.kubernetes.io/instance` which is not present in current per-µservice selectors (would add a label, not strip — same outcome as J-3). slice_j3_kustomize.honest_finding: The canonical namespace-restricted-profile component, as authored by Sweep-I, bundled a placeholder namespace.yaml + serviceaccount.yaml as `resources:`. Composing this component into per-µservice base/kustomization.yaml would CONFLICT with the per-µservice namespace.yaml (which carries µservice-specific labels like oyatie.dev/microservice, oyatie.dev/invariants, oyatie/owning-axis). Migrated the component from `bundle resources` pattern to `commonLabels overlay only` pattern — removed the two placeholder files. Per-µservice base files surveyed (30): zero base has duplicate istio-injection or pod-security-restricted labels in commonLabels (these labels live in per-µservice namespace.yaml metadata.labels, NOT in kustomize commonLabels). Per-µservice overlays surveyed (67): zero overlay has duplicate commonAnnotations (oyatie/pack, oyatie/jurisdiction, oyatie/region) matching pack-overlay-canonical/<pack> — overlays use configMapGenerator with per-µservice literal keys + µservice-specific patches; canonical's commonAnnotations are ADDITIVE not deduplicative. Conclusion: composing the canonical components would ADD canonical metadata, not strip duplicates. That is a harmonize-pack-annotations task (separate IP), not a strip task. Target ~2,000 lines removed was based on aspirational assumption that overlays carried boilerplate duplication; reality is they don't.
